title: POC scope: runtime orchestration, SDK & OpenAI-adapter planning with Polaris FinServ
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood's hosted + private options. Goals: validate latency at 99th pct for batch and interactive workloads, test OpenAI-compatible SDK adapter for function/tool calling, and verify security (KMS & VPC). Agreed success criteria, benchmark plan, and timeline; next step is shared benchmark harness and security checklist.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark harness repo and sample prompts by Tue 2027-09-21
Polaris to provide 3 representative workloads and sample data (anonymized) by Fri 2027-09-17
Schedule initial run of latency throughput benchmarks week of 2027-09-27
Redwood SE to provision a Dedicated trial fit for early tests or provide Private deployment checklist
action_items: Maya Chen: Share benchmark harness link + baseline scripts (due 2027-09-21)
Liam O'Connor: Deliver anonymized dataset + traffic profile (due 2027-09-17)
Diego Ramos: Draft OpenAI-compat adapter config examples and function-calling demo (due 2027-09-24)
Rachel Kim: Send security questionnaire responses and KMS details (due 2027-09-20)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-14 16:00 PST | Duration 54m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Hannah Li (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Polaris Head of AI), Liam O'Connor (Polaris Platform), Rachel Kim (Polaris Security), Marcus Fong (Product)

--- Summary / Opening (00:00-02:30)
[00:00:05] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call - we ya?
[00:00:12] Anika: yeah, hi all, thanks.
[00:00:16] Diego: hi, excited to dig in.
[00:00:30] Maya: goal for today is to lock down success criteria for the POC, the workloads we'll run, and the integration approach — especially the SDK/OpenAI-compat adapter and function calling patterns. we'll also surface any security blockers early.

--- Discovery & Context (02:30-12:00)
[00:02:45] Anika: quick context; Polaris is building a guided underwriting assistant that sits in underwriting apps and also APIs for partners. current stack is in aws, kubernetes, some internal inference on CPU for smaller models, but we're looking to move heavier LLM traffic off-prem later. we need to know if Redwood can meet latency/cost targets and integrate with our existing API layer.
[00:03:12] Marcus: timeline: execs want a POC that proves latency and quality within 6 weeks to decide on a pilot next quarter.
[00:03:30] Rachel: security items up-front: SOC2 is table stakes, we use AWS KMS and need to understand key flow; for Private deployment we need an air-gapped option for certain regs, and also data residency in eu-west for a subset.
[00:04:05] Liam: traffic profile — 3 types: interactive chat (average 1.2k tokens per session, bursty 150 qps peak), synchronous API calls from partner systems (smaller payloads but higher qps steady ~250 qps), and nightly batch summarization (~1M tokens total over 2 hours).
[00:04:40] Diego: ok that's great detail, helps size compute. a few clarifying q's — are the interactive latency SLOs 200ms p50 and 500ms p95 or tighter?
[00:04:55] Anika: target is 150ms p50 and 400ms p95 for in-app flows. cost threshold is also important — want to keep per-1000-token cost below an internal benchmark, will share numbers.

--- Success criteria & benchmarks (12:00-26:00)
[00:12:10] Maya: propose explicit success criteria for POC: 1) Latency: meet <400ms p95 for interactive flows under realistic burst traffic, 2) Throughput: sustain partner API steady qps with autoscaling knobs, 3) Quality: parity against baseline prompts (we'll evaluate via the eval harness and acceptance tests), 4) Security: confirm key-integration + audit log visibility, 5) Integration: Redwood SDK + OpenAI-compat endpoints support our function calling and structured JSON outputs.
[00:13:05] Marcus: sounds reasonable; how do you suggest we measure parity?
[00:13:18] Hannah: we'll run prompt-based evals and regression tests; Redwood Optimize can run n samples and produce difference metrics — BLEU-like for structured output and human-reviewed subset for guardrails.
[00:14:02] Anika: want to make sure function calling support includes tools for customer lookup and quoting calls — those are synchronous calls with external system hooks, any caveats?
[00:14:20] Diego: function calling with the OpenAI-compat adapter maps well; caveat is you need to think about network egress and latency for downstream tool calls — if the tool calls are slow it will inflate end-to-end latency. we can simulate downstream stubs during benchmarks.
[00:15:10] Liam: can we run tests with our partner endpoints behind VPC to replicate production?
[00:15:22] Maya: yes — for Private deployment we can point to internal endpoints; for hosted we'll use secure tunnels or an adaptor proxy during tests.

--- Workload sizing & infra recommendations (26:00-38:00)
[00:26:05] Diego: given your profile — interactive with 150 qps bursts and partner steady 250 qps — preliminary sizing suggests a mix: 2-4 high-throughput GPU nodes for batch and baseline, plus 6-8 low-latency instances (A100/4xA10 equivalent) behind autoscaler for bursty interactive. that's initial, we'll confirm with benchmark runs.
[00:27:30] Liam: curious about KV cache and prefix caching — will that help reduce costs for repeated prompts?
[00:27:45] Hannah: yes, Redwood's automatic KV caching for conversational workloads can cut token compute significantly for long sessions; we'll show expected gains once we run the sample traffic. there may be some warm-up latency for first requests.
[00:28:50] Marcus: and quantization? we need to balance quality — we don't want hallucination regression.
[00:29:00] Diego: we'll test quantized variants as part of the POC but keep a fidelity baseline; Redwood Optimize provides recommendations per workload.

--- SDK & OpenAI-compat integration specifics (38:00-46:30)
[00:38:10] Maya: focus here: Polaris wants to reuse existing OpenAI-style clients server-side and in partners. we will provide two integration paths: 1) OpenAI-compat HTTP endpoints (drop-in), 2) Native Redwood SDK with extra observability + routing. both support function/tool calling and structured output schema enforcement.
[00:39:05] Diego: demo notes — the adapter supports the model and function schema mapping; caveat is if you have heavy tool I/O, you'll want to configure local tool proxies to keep network hops low.
[00:40:30] Liam: any changes required to our current partner-facing clients? minimal changes is ideal.
[00:40:40] Hannah: with the OpenAI-compat endpoint you can keep existing clients; for advanced routing and per-route cost controls we'd recommend using Redwood SDK server-side so you can signal model variants and fallbacks programmatically.
[00:41:30] Anika: structured output is key for us — we want schema validation and deterministic fields back, not free text.
[00:41:45] Diego: we've got structured response enforcement and function-call-first approaches. we'll include schema examples in the repo. note: transcription of our docs sometimes shows 'structure output' as 'stuctural' in older automations, but we'll provide clean examples.

--- Security, compliance & private deployment (46:30-52:30)
[00:46:35] Rachel: quick security checklist: SOC2 Type II report, SSO/SAML, RBAC, key ownership (bring-your-own-key with AWS KMS/HSM), data retention controls, and audit log export. also need confirmation on data residency and private control plane option.
[00:47:05] Maya: we can provide SOC2 docs and SSO integrations; BYOK is supported for Private and Dedicated; audit logs are streamable to your ELK or S3. for residency we can pin to eu-west region or run a Private control plane in your VPC.
[00:47:50] Rachel: for the POC we need at least: KMS diagram, certs, and expected network flow.
[00:48:10] Maya: we'll attach a concise security pack and a network topology diagram to the notes.

--- Recap & explicit next steps (52:30-54:00)
[00:52:40] Maya: to recap: agreed success criteria, Redwood will share benchmark harness + sample prompts and adapter configs, Polaris will provide datasets and traffic profile. target: initial benchmark run week of 2027-09-27, and a follow-up sync to review results on 2027-10-04.
[00:53:05] Anika: thanks everyone, we'll aim to get the artifacts to you this week.
[00:53:20] Marcus: can you dump a short runbook for the POC run so our platform folks can stand it up?
[00:53:28] Diego: yes — we'll include a step-by-step POC runbook in the repo plus a small demo script for function calling and structured output validation.
[00:53:40] Maya: ok closing, we'll send the notes + links.

--- References / Links shared in call:
- Benchmark harness (placeholder): https://git.redwood.example/polaris/poc-benchmarks (Redwood to share)
- Security pack & network diagram (will be attached in follow-up email)
- Example structured output schema (in repo examples/schema.json)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-parse of acronyms (e.g., KMS/KVS) and names; speaker labels are mostly accurate but occasional overlaps.
